text:
Alicia (SRE): paging — post-deploy we’re seeing a surge of 429s from the rate limiter, customers reporting blocked requests. deploy-bot: Canary deployment finished at ~+12m with no immediate failures.
Matt (Infra): curious — telemetry shows a sudden jump in RL rejections at 10:07 UTC in eu-west-1, looks correlated with the rollout.
Neeraj (API): stack says exemptions lookup is returning empty for a subset of tokens. Not every user, seems tied to tokens issued before 2024-12-01.
Lina (Support): we have 3 enterprise tickets from EU customers — they’re seeing sustained failures for embed endpoints. Escalating to SEs.
Alicia (SRE): tagging @Jorge to look at the canary config. Did the new ratecap change the exemptions lookup key?
Jorge (Eng): I pushed the canary that updates the ratecap code path and cached exemptions under key `exemptions:v2`. Turned on feature flag `rl_exemptions_v2`.
Neeraj (API): confirm — the runtime uses `exemptions:v1` in primary and `exemptions:v2` as fallback. Looks like fallback path is skipped when the flag is set.
Alicia (SRE): immediate mitigation: can we flip the feature flag off (rollback the flag) while we investigate? This is customer-impacting.
Matt (Infra): I'm on it. Running:
```bash
# flip flag via console API
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://flags.redwood/api/flags/rl_exemptions_v2 -d '{"state":"off"}'
```
deploy-bot: Feature flag rl_exemptions_v2 set to OFF by Matt (Infra)
Alicia (SRE): nice, monitor metrics. Lina, ask SEs to confirm if customer requests recover.
Lina (Support): on it. SEs confirm initial recovery for org-827 and org-99 within 2 mins. Still seeing intermittent 429s for org-410.
Neeraj (API): digging in logs — org-410 tokens are hitting a different auth shard that failed to roll the fallback code correctly. There's a race where cached key lookup returns nil and code treats it as non-exempt.
Alicia (SRE): impact estimate?
Neeraj (API): approx 1.8% of global requests, concentrated eu-west-1 and us-east-1 edges. Top affected customers: org-827, org-410, org-99.
Jorge (Eng): root cause: the canary introduced a path that assumes `exemptions:v2` exists for all shards. Canary ran on 20% of hosts but the feature flag cascaded client-side causing some requests to hit v2-only path on non-upgraded shards.
oncall-next: taking handoff in 15.
Alicia (SRE): actions so far: 1) rolled back flag 2) notified SEs 3) created incident. Need long-term fix: make exemptions lookup backward compatible and add a canary gate to avoid mixed-path state.
Matt (Infra): we also applied a temporary routing policy to favor upgraded hosts while we clean up caches. Policy rule: prefer host group `rl-canary-true` -> reduced error rate by ~60%.
Lina (Support): CS wants a customer message. Draft: "We experienced an intermittent rate-limiting issue affecting a small subset of requests in EU/US. A fix was deployed and rolled back; affected customers should see normal service. We're following up with root cause and safeguards." Approve? :thumbsup:
Alicia (SRE): thumbs. Add: "If you continue to see issues please DM support with request ids."
Neeraj (API): collecting repro steps and logs; will open a follow-up PR to make the lookup tolerant: fallback to v1 when v2 missing plus assert checks in canary.
Jorge (Eng): proposed patch:
```diff
- exemptions = cache.get("exemptions:v2")
- if exemptions == nil { // assume non-exempt }
+ exemptions = cache.get("exemptions:v2")
+ if exemptions == nil {
+   // fallback to v1 to be backwards compatible
+   exemptions = cache.get("exemptions:v1")
+ }
```
Alicia (SRE): add metric and alert when `v2` misses spike > 0.1% of requests during rollout.
Matt (Infra): note — token-accounting logs show ~120k requests reclassified; cost impact negligible but customer impact real.
Lina (Support): SEs will follow up with the three customers and offer a postmortem link.
deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3849 — post-deploy exemptions mismatch -> over-throttle. Pager sent.
pagerduty-bot: Acknowledged by Alicia (SRE).
oncall-next: taking over. Alicia handing off, summary: flag-off mitigated majority, routing policy reduced errors further, root cause is canary + missing backward compatibility on exemptions cache, next steps include PR, canary gating, enhanced monitors, customer comms.
Alicia (SRE): handing off full incident doc to oncall-next. I'll join postmortem.
oncall-next: acknowledged — we'll run the patch through a small canary with explicit gating and monitor for `exemptions:v2` miss-rate and 429s.
Lina (Support): creating a KB article for customer-facing notes and tagging affected accounts.
Alicia (SRE): postmortem tasks: 1) fix code fallback and add unit tests 2) add rollout gate that waits until all shards report `v2` present 3) add alert for v2-miss spikes 4) coordinate with CS on customer outreach.
Neeraj (API): ETA for PR and canary? 2 hours for PR + tests, canary after code review within 4 hours.
Jorge (Eng): will add canary verification script: it polls cache keys across shards and fails rollout if inconsistent.
Alicia (SRE): OK. Closing immediate pager. If anything regresses @channel — reopen. :white_check_mark:
